context_requirements: Cell must express one or more adenosine receptor subtypes (ADORA1, ADORA2A, ADORA2B, ADORA3) at sufficient levels.
Adenosine tone must be present, either endogenous or generated in the assay, for antagonism to reduce basal receptor signaling.
Adenosine A2A/A2B-mediated cAMP/PKA signaling should be active to observe reversal of its transcriptional effects.
For antiproliferative effects, cells should be dependent on adenosine-driven proliferation or survival signals.
falsifiers: No consistent change in cAMP-responsive immediate early genes (FOS, JUN, EGR1) at 6 h across responsive lines.
No reduction in proliferation-associated genes (e.g., CCNA2, CCNB1, CDK1) at 24 h in any line.
Strong and uniform upregulation of generic stress or interferon programs at 6 h, which would suggest off-target effects rather than adenosine receptor antagonism.
Lack of any transcriptional response in A549 or HT29, which are expected to express adenosine receptors and show moderate responses.
